producer_report.summary: Root cause: reading acceptance never compared the reading's references with the snapshot, so a reading saying an earlier job's file, role or prompt already exists was accepted. The earlier job could be queued, unmerged or never produced, and the critic found the gap later. I added `check_reading_references` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. It runs last in `check_reading_acceptance`. It scans the summary, assumptions and acceptance criteria for repo paths under a top-level directory of the snapshot (or crates, docs, xtask, studies, .github). It refuses any path that is not in the base commit's files, not a create deliverable (or a directory above one), not CHANGELOG.md, and not in a sentence that says it is absent or to be created. The message names each path and field and tells the reader to list it as a create deliverable or say it does not exist. With no file set, or a reading that declines or asks a question, it checks nothing. It is deterministic and keys on no job id. Four new unit tests cover refusal, acceptance, different absent paths and the repair text. I added a CHANGELOG.md entry and D147 in docs/decisions.md. Clippy, fmt, the policy scan and the full test run all passed.

Without the call, check_reading_acceptance would return Ok and the unwrap_err would panic. I did not run it with the check removed.

open_issues: Bare root file names (Cargo.lock) and slash-less basenames are deliberately not checked, as the plan said. Say so if the user wants them checked.
The share of readings newly refused (expected about 3%) was not measured: there is no stored-reading replay set with file sets.
The absence-phrase list is a judgment, and one phrase in a sentence exempts every path in that sentence.
I did not run `cargo test --locked` with the check removed, so the claim that the new tests fail without it rests on reading the code.
mistakes: The first tokenizer checked for `..` after trimming trailing dots, so an ellipsis path (`crates/athena-core/...`) became the existing `crates/athena-core` and my test passed for the wrong reason. I fixed it to test the untrimmed run.
The first version of the new test used a function-pointer array type that clippy rejected as too complex. I replaced it with a local alias.
learnings: `check_reading_acceptance` is called in production only from `read_for`, which passes the base commit's `ls_tree` paths as repo_files. Other tests call `check_boundary_and_repo_files` directly with None, so they are unaffected.
Clippy denies a `[(&str, fn(&mut Reading, String)); N]` type as too complex; the existing tests use a local `type Edit` alias.
A file path starting with `.github` begins with a dot, so the tokenizer must skip only `./`, not every leading dot.
desires: A way to read the saved output of a long cargo test run inside the working directory, to count passing tests.
